findings.title: Async-buffer drain-complete has no named watchable signal for the abort sequence
findings.detail: Section 7.2 step 2 instructs the operator to 'flip the capture flag off and confirm in-flight async-buffer writes have drained' before proceeding to snapshot. The drain-confirmation has no named instrument at CHG altitude: no queue-depth metric, no drain-complete log event, no health endpoint. Section 4.1 signal (4) is a drop-rate counter — a lagging accumulator — and does not indicate buffer-empty. The reasoning-frame principle (paragraph 3) is that an abort step that depends on an observation the operator cannot make deterministically is inoperable under incident pressure. A CHG-altitude pointer such as 'drain-complete confirmed via buffer-depth metric or drain-complete log event, authored in SPEC-02' would close the gap without over-specifying thresholds. As written, the operator has no named instrument to determine when step 2 is satisfied before proceeding to steps 3-4.
